f1.quote: Systematically substituted Co for Ni by increasing x from 0.40 to 0.55

f2.quote: annealed at 750 °C for 72 h in high vacuum, and water-quenched

f3.quote: DSC was performed from 183–400 K at 10 K min−1 under N2

f4.quote: isothermal magnetization/entropy measurements used fields up to 5 T near TC

f5.quote: strengthened/stabilized the high-temperature hexagonal Ni2In-type phase, shifted the hexagonal-to-orthorhombic TiNiSi-type transformation downward

f6.quote: changed the transition from coupled first-order magnetostructural behavior for x = 0.40–0.50 to a second-order magnetic transition for x = 0.55

f7.quote: When the structural transition lies near TC, coupling between ferromagnetic TiNiSi-type martensite and paramagnetic Ni2In-type austenite produces latent heat, hysteresis, and a giant magnetocaloric response; loss of this coupling at x = 0.55 yields a small second-order response.

f8.quote: Relative to the low-Co x = 0.40 alloy, increasing Co substitution was found to progressively lower Ttr, TC, and peak magnetic entropy change, eventually suppressing the giant first-order magnetocaloric effect at x = 0.55

f12.quote: while generally increasing hardness and giving the highest compressive strength at x = 0.55
